study_title: Daigneault et al., review of behavioural benefit-take-up field experiments
comparator_and_sample: 35 field studies / 93 interventions
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Effects heterogeneous; some information and assistance approaches promising
important_limitation: Review overlap with E04; largely US; no pooled meta-analysis
followup_duration: review spans approximately 20 years of studies

study_title: Bendtsen, Increasing Take-Up of Social Benefits
comparator_and_sample: 51 field-experimental studies / 187 effects
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: 51 studies; 187 effects. Receipt effects: compliance-help +8.31pp versus information/learning-demand +3.39pp on average; applications easier to shift
important_limitation: Review overlaps E03 and primary trials; estimates not portable

study_title: Finkelstein and Notowidigdo, Take-Up and Targeting: SNAP
comparator_and_sample: Information; information plus application help; status quo
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: 6% control; 11% information; 18% information plus help
important_limitation: Likely-eligible older adults; institutional targeting and labour intensity
study_cost: Hands-on assistance resource intensity not extracted

study_title: Giannella et al., Administrative Burden and Procedural Denials
comparator_and_sample: Flexible applicant-initiated interviews versus usual SNAP process
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Approvals +6 percentage points; long-term participation over +2pp
important_limitation: 65k applicants; single agency; procedural context
followup_duration: Long-term participation endpoint reported; exact duration not checked

study_title: Castell et al., Take-up of Social Benefits
comparator_and_sample: Social worker meeting and eligibility simulator versus control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: In-person assistance +29% relative take-up; online simulator no significant effect
important_limitation: Jobseeker sample; attendance selection and French institutions

study_title: Linos et al., Can Nudges Increase Take-Up of the EITC?
comparator_and_sample: Messages versus usual tax filing
measured_endpoint: Actual EITC claims and tax returns
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: No detectable change in filing or claiming despite one million observations
important_limitation: Low-touch nudges; non-filers; not a test of intensive assistance

study_title: Domenella et al., Non-take-up: in-person and digital outreach
comparator_and_sample: In-person and social-media outreach versus untreated tracts
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Applications rose; no robust increase in approvals
important_limitation: 400 census tracts; follow-up burden; eligibility uncertainty
followup_duration: During treatment and 1-6 months after; see publisher source
adverse_or_equity_effects: Unapproved applications increase process burden; data on actual net benefits unavailable

study_title: Interventions to bolster benefits take-up: outreach framing
comparator_and_sample: Tax-benefit outreach messages versus usual outreach
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Light-touch outreach +0.14 to 2 percentage points take-up in targeted settings
important_limitation: COVID-era child tax credit/stimulus; modest absolute effects; external validity

study_title: Martin et al., ACA marketplace enrollment interventions
comparator_and_sample: Interventions versus no/usual outreach across studies
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Mean marketplace enrolment +0.9pp across reviewed trials; assistance +2.0pp and information +0.6pp
important_limitation: Health insurance enrollment; mix of 32 RCTs and 2 quasi studies; overlapping component trials
study_cost: Support intensity higher; costs not extracted

study_title: De La Rosa et al., Psychological ownership government benefits
comparator_and_sample: Ownership-framing messages versus comparators
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Interest in claiming benefits increased under ownership framing
important_limitation: Interest and navigation not evidence of verified receipt; mechanism context

study_title: Fowlie et al., Do Energy Efficiency Investments Deliver?
comparator_and_sample: Weatherisation programme versus comparison
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Realised energy savings substantially below models; investment about twice private energy savings; no significant indoor-temperature gain
important_limitation: Particular US programme; health/carbon externalities separately assessed
study_cost: Capital investment approximately twice realised private energy savings

study_title: McAndrew et al., Household energy efficiency interventions
comparator_and_sample: 153 interventions in 160 papers
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Review finds heterogeneous effects; combined strategies often more successful
important_limitation: Variable outcomes and study quality; not all low-income households

study_title: Systematic Review of Energy Efficiency Home Retrofit Evaluation Studies
comparator_and_sample: 39 evaluations of 23 retrofit programmes
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Average savings roughly 7.2%; no programme reached 50% savings in included sample
important_limitation: Overlapping programmes; mixed designs; bill savings not equal to wellbeing

study_title: Financial support and fuel poverty health outcomes
comparator_and_sample: 20 evaluated interventions including one RCT and before-after studies
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Many studies report improved warmth or wellbeing, but large design heterogeneity
important_limitation: Predominantly nonrandomised studies; causal strength varies; cost uncertainty

study_title: Energy coaching and fix-team retrofitting
comparator_and_sample: Intervention applicants treated versus waiting-list applicants
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Fix teams associated with improved perceived comfort and financial concerns
important_limitation: Self-selection; nonrandom groups; survey outcomes; short follow-up

study_title: EJUSTA energy counselling quasi-experimental evaluation
comparator_and_sample: Counselling and tariff help versus convenience comparison group
measured_endpoint: Energy poverty and health at one year
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Local counselling assessed; causal effects and full estimates require full-text extraction
important_limitation: Convenience comparison group; selection bias; do not extrapolate

study_title: Non-price conservation information and consumption RCT
comparator_and_sample: Conservation advice and neighbour comparisons versus control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Expert conservation advice reduced electricity use and bills in trial
important_limitation: Affordability vs suppressed consumption and welfare not established

study_title: Impact evaluation of the social electricity tariff
comparator_and_sample: Households around income eligibility cutoff
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Near cutoff spending lower by R$15.35 monthly and consumption lower by 20kWh
important_limitation: Local discontinuity and possible underconsumption; cannot claim improved comfort

study_title: Bagnoli and Bertomeu-Sanchez, social electricity rate
comparator_and_sample: Eligibility before/after 2009 introduction versus comparison
measured_endpoint: Likelihood of energy poverty and electricity spending
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Small reduction in energy-poverty probability; lower bills without higher use
important_limitation: Parallel-trends and household eligibility assumptions need full text

study_title: Searle et al., Structural improvements and energy poverty
comparator_and_sample: Households experiencing different local measures over time
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Structural measures and financial help associated with better outcomes; small advice mixed
important_limitation: Not randomised; self reports; attribution confounded by policy and site

study_title: Howden-Chapman et al., Insulating houses and health inequality
comparator_and_sample: Retrofitted insulation versus deferred installation
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Bedroom warmth +0.5°C and lower energy use in intervention households
important_limitation: Multi-outcome trial; original health and utilisation endpoints need fuller extraction
confidence_interval: Study abstract gives +0.5°C bedroom temperature; CI not extracted

study_title: Howden-Chapman et al., Improved heating for children with asthma
comparator_and_sample: Effective low-pollution heater versus deferred provision
measured_endpoint: Respiratory symptoms and school days; lung function
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Reduced symptoms and school absence; lung function change nonsignificant
important_limitation: Health-targeted households; not direct proof of lower energy bills
confidence_interval: Living-room temperature +1.10°C (95% CI 0.54 to 1.64); FEV1 mean difference 130.7ml (95% CI -20.3 to 281.7)
adverse_or_equity_effects: Lung-function difference statistically nonsignificant; asthma-targeted rather than representative of general poverty

study_title: Banerjee et al., Multifaceted graduation programme
comparator_and_sample: Asset transfer plus coaching/savings/consumption support versus control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Consumption improved in five of six sites; benefits exceeded cost in five
important_limitation: Bundled intervention; different country contexts and delivery costs
followup_duration: Approximately one year after programme conclusion; 3 years from asset transfer
study_cost: Programme benefits exceeded costs in five of six study sites

study_title: Blattman et al., Generating skilled self-employment
comparator_and_sample: Grant for training and assets versus no grant
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: At year four earnings +38%; business assets +57%
important_limitation: Young applicants in post-conflict region; same trial as later E? follow-up

study_title: Blattman et al., Nine-year youth grants follow-up
comparator_and_sample: Same experiment as 2014 grants paper
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Earlier earnings gain faded; treated and controls converged
important_limitation: NOT an independent trial from 2014; long-run attrition and context
adverse_or_equity_effects: Income convergence at long horizon; same original Uganda trial as earlier 2014 record

study_title: Alfonsi et al., Tackling youth unemployment
comparator_and_sample: Vocational training vs firm training vs control
measured_endpoint: Employment skills and earnings four years
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Both improved jobs; vocational training effects arose more slowly and lasted longer
important_limitation: Urban youth and firm selection; training intensity and cost
study_cost: Vocational training versus firm-provided training costs not extracted

study_title: Blattman et al., Returns to microenterprise support
comparator_and_sample: Cash and business training/supervision versus control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: At 16 months microenterprise ownership and incomes roughly doubled
important_limitation: War-affected women; heterogeneous effects; package not unbundled

study_title: Bandiera et al., Search for Good Jobs
comparator_and_sample: Vocational training; matching; both versus control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Vocational training raised outcomes; additional matching sometimes worsened search and job quality
important_limitation: Same cohort interventions within single experiment; employer selection
adverse_or_equity_effects: Light-touch job matching discouraged some trainees and lowered job quality compared with training only

study_title: Blattman and Dercon, Industrial and entrepreneurial work
comparator_and_sample: Factory job offer vs entrepreneurship package vs control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Factory offers no durable earnings gain and increased health risks; business package earnings +33%
important_limitation: Five firms; attrition and local factory conditions
adverse_or_equity_effects: Industrial placements increased health problems; many employees quit

study_title: Can a light-touch graduation model enhance livelihood outcomes?
comparator_and_sample: Cash or poultry plus training/savings versus reduced bundle and control
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Some livestock/asset gains; no detectable consumption improvement
important_limitation: May not cross poverty trap; targeted population and programme dose

study_title: Bandiera et al., Labor Markets and Poverty in Village Economies
comparator_and_sample: Livestock/skills package versus comparison households
measured_endpoint: Earnings and poverty through seven years
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Increases in earnings and asset accumulation sustained at years four and seven
important_limitation: Strong programme-support context; nonparticipants and markets matter

study_title: Brown et al., Financial incentives for apprenticeship trainers
comparator_and_sample: Performance incentive to trainers versus fixed participation pay
measured_endpoint: Apprentice skills and earnings two years
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Apprentice earnings +24% and skills +0.15SD two years later
important_limitation: Trainer incentive trial; does not identify effects of apprenticeship access itself

study_title: McKenzie, Active labor market policy critical review
comparator_and_sample: Evaluations of training, job assistance and wage subsidies
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Many programmes have small or no significant gains
important_limitation: Narrative review; overlapping with later review; varies by policy

study_title: Carranza and McKenzie, Job Training and Job Search Assistance
comparator_and_sample: Cross-study policy evaluations
measured_endpoint: Job training and job matching outcomes
finding_verified_from_abstract_or_summar: Typical impacts often small; context and cost-effectiveness critical
important_limitation: Review overlaps McKenzie 2017 and individual trials
